correctness.rationale: Parity Fourier transform gives \(A(z)=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-a&1\\z&-b\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), with \(\operatorname{tr}(A(z)^*A(z))=S\) and \(\det(A(z)^*A(z))=|ab-z|^2\). On the unit circle, the least determinant is \(\delta^2\) and the smaller singular-value square is \((S-\sqrt{S^2-4\delta^2})/2\). Rationalization yields the stated sharp inverse norm. The singular phase when \(r=1\) destroys any lower bound. The arithmetic-geometric mean argument gives the unique fixed-product optimum. Uniqueness of the minimizing phase when \(ab\ne0\) yields nonattainment by the positive-measure criterion, whereas \(ab=0\) gives a measurable maximizing singular-vector field. The proof covers all complex parameters and quantified inputs.

value.rationale: This is a complete sharp stability profile, not a chosen numeric example: the canonical two-periodic first-order recurrence admits exact ℓ2 residual-error constants for all complex coefficients, including zero. It distinguishes two recurrences with identical Floquet multiplier but arbitrarily different energy stability, identifies the unique balanced optimum, and classifies actual norm attainment. This gives a natural quantitative robustness invariant not implied by the one-sided pointwise literature. Its norm geometry matters in perturbation/error assessment across heterogeneous periodic steps.
